alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 7 at 10:53AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 AM EST Saturday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:15 AM EST Saturday was 16.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 16.9 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 6 at 11:56PM EST until November 9 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches of Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

advisories.text: Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa (9 miles west) in Brevard County: at 7:15 PM Friday the river stood at 16.9 feet, above the 16.0-foot flood stage, and moderate flooding is happening now. NWS now expects the river to stay steady at about 16.9 feet and still says major flooding is forecast. The warning stays in effect until further notice. At 17.2 feet the Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.

advisories.agency: National Weather Service Melbourne / Brevard County Emergency Management (via News 6 WKMG)
advisories.text: In written answers to News 6 on Friday, NWS Melbourne said the St. Johns River near Cocoa should crest at about 17.1 feet around Tuesday or Wednesday, November 10–11. That is above the 17-foot major flood stage. At 17.2 feet, Providence Road west of Cocoa can become impassable, which could cut off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road areas. River forecasts can change. Brevard County Emergency Management is warning residents west of I-95 and along flood-prone parts of the St. Johns River to watch for flooding in low-lying areas. Do not drive through flooded roads.

Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa (9 miles west) in Brevard County, issued at 10:53 AM Saturday: at 10:15 AM Saturday the river stood at 16.9 feet, above the 16.0-foot flood stage. The highest level in the 24 hours before that reading was also 16.9 feet. NWS expects the river to stay steady at about 16.9 feet and still says major flooding is forecast. The warning stays in effect. At 17.2 feet the Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Use caution near the riverbanks and do not drive through flooded areas.
